surprises.description: Herc reported adjusted EPS of $3.91, far above the preview’s $2.92 consensus estimate. That is a much larger result than the preview’s view that EPS risk skewed down.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted net income was $131 million or $3.91 per diluted share.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. diluted EPS | Q3'26 Consensus: $2.92”; “EPS risk is skewed down.”

surprises.description: Herc raised its full-year equipment rental revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, rather than holding the existing ranges as the preview’s base case anticipated. The new midpoints are about 2% above the prior guidance midpoints.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised full-year guidance to midpoint equipment rental revenue of $4.513 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $2.13 billion, up about 2% from prior guidance.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Base (50%) ... FY guide reaffirmed at midpoint”; “Watch whether the $4.375–4.475B ERR range is narrowed up, held, or trimmed.”

surprises.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 44.2%, expanding 190 basis points, above the preview’s implied margin of about 43.5% and roughly 120 basis points of expected year-over-year expansion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA rose about 9% with margin expanding 190 basis points to 44.2%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA margin | ~43.5% (implied)”; the preview said the margin needed to be “up ~120bps YoY.”

surprises.description: Dollar utilization rose 360 basis points year over year, well above the preview’s 40.3%+ level for confirming fleet absorption. The preview identified local-market weakness and a sub-40% utilization result as concerns.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Dollar utilization up 360 basis points in the quarter.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A print of 40.3%+ confirms the fleet is being absorbed”; “sub-40% says HRI is buying revenue with capex.”

surprises.description: Net fleet CapEx guidance rose to about $1.05 billion at the midpoint, above the preview’s $850–950 million net rental CapEx range. Some of the increase is a pull-forward of specialty fleet spending for committed mega projects, rather than entirely new 2026 spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net fleet CapEx guidance was increased to approximately $1.05 billion at the midpoint, with roughly $150 million representing specialty fleet effectively pulled forward from the 2027 budget for committed mega projects.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net rental capex | $850–950M”; the preview flagged “leverage and capex discipline” as a key issue.

surprises.description: Herc disclosed that CEO Larry Silber will become Executive Chairman and that long-time President and COO Aaron Birnbaum will become CEO on January 1. The preview did not anticipate or discuss a leadership transition.
surprises.fact_evidence: “CEO Larry Silber will transition to Executive Chairman on January 1, with President and COO Aaron Birnbaum (35+ year Herc veteran) stepping in as CEO.”

surprises.description: Herc raised its targeted mega-project rental share to 20% from a prior 15% top end, a more ambitious long-term goal than the preview discussed. Management cautioned that this is a multi-year journey and not expected to be achieved in 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company raised its targeted mega project rental share goal to 20% (from a prior 15% top end), framed as a multi-year journey not expected to be reached in 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the “2027 framing” was important and its base case assumed “no 2027 numbers,” but did not anticipate a higher mega-project share target.

surprises.description: Alongside adjusted EBITDA margin expansion, REBITDA margin fell 70 basis points to 45% as fuel, freight, operating-cost inflation and higher field incentives outweighed pricing and H&E synergy benefits. That signals more cost pressure than the preview’s margin-improvement and synergy-realization case suggested, though REBITDA margin is a separate measure.
surprises.fact_evidence: “REBITDA margin fell 70 basis points to 45% as fuel, freight, operating cost inflation and higher field incentive compensation outweighed pricing and H&E synergy benefits.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said the quarter should show the $125M synergy program becoming visible and that adjusted EBITDA margin was implied at “~43.5%,” up about 120 basis points year over year.
